ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17, and Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, ss. 462.31 and 462.33; Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, ss. 21.1–21.5; Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9, including significant-control and corporate-records provisions.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority or notary public in the owner's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; if the source state is not an Apostille party, consular legalization at the Canadian embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential address (recent utility bill or bank statement, issued within 90 days)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or financial institution in the beneficial owner's country of residence; notarized by a local notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; if the source state is not an Apostille party, consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney or corporate resolution appointing an Alberta registered agent and incorporation representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate shareholder's board of directors or secretary, certified by a notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; if the source state is not an Apostille party, consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or certified corporate extract for any corporate beneficial owner

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commissioner for oaths or notary public in the country of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarization if executed in Canada; Hague Apostille if executed abroad and submitted for Canadian registration

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners against Global Affairs Canada's Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, and FINTRAC's Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) criteria. Enhanced due diligence applies where any UBO or director is a domestic or foreign PEP, a head of an international organization, or is ordinarily resident outside Canada. Repeated screening is required every 90 days and immediately upon any material change in ownership. OFAC SDN screening is additionally required where USD-denominated wire transfers or US correspondent banking rails are used.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry – Online Name Search and Reservation Service (Service Alberta, Government of Alberta)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed corporate name must be expressed in English or French using Latin-alphabet characters; any name originating in a non-Latin script requires an official transliteration. The name must include a legal element such as Limited, Ltd., Incorporated, Inc., Corporation, or Corp., and must be distinguishable from existing names in the Alberta corporate registry and in the federal NUANS database.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Director of Corporate Registry rejects a proposed name, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with Service Alberta within 30 days of the rejection notice. The appeal must include the original name-search report, a statutory declaration explaining the grounds for distinctiveness, and an amended proposed name. The Director may approve or reject the amended name, and the applicant retains the right to judicial review of that decision in the Court of King's Bench of Alberta.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office and mail-forwarding address is permissible for operational correspondence but may not be used as the corporation's registered office. The registered office must be a physical street address in Alberta where legal process can be served; a post office box is prohibited. For a matcha powder distribution company, commercial substance can be satisfied by maintaining the registered office plus an operational sales office, warehousing arrangement, or third-party fulfillment facility in Alberta or in another Canadian province where business activities occur.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated low-to-moderate risk. Unannounced corporate-registry physical inspections are rare and generally occur only upon reasonable belief of non-compliance, with an estimated probability of less than 2%. If matcha powder is imported and stored in a Canada Border Services Agency or Canadian Food Inspection Agency regulated facility, the probability of an unannounced visit increases to approximately 5-10% absent red flags, and to 40-60% if food-safety complaints, customs holds, or record-keeping deficiencies are present.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, ss. 8-21 (incorporation, registered office, share capital), s. 25 (consideration for shares), s. 101 (directors), s. 105 (officers); Alberta Companies Regulation, Alta Reg 77/2021 (filing fees); alternative federal regime: Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Service Alberta - Alberta Corporate Registry, including accredited Registry Agents and the ORGOnline electronic filing portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Alberta Form A-1) filed together with Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the Alberta Business Corporations Act. A private corporation may be incorporated with one shareholder and one director; shares may be issued for money, property, or past services under s. 25, and no escrow account or capital deposit is required by the Alberta Corporate Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION (Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9). RESOLVED: (1) The share subscription agreement be accepted and 100 Class A common shares be allotted and issued to the sole subscriber in exchange for contributed paid-up capital. (2) The registered office at 000 X Avenue NW, Calgary, Alberta, Canada T0A 0A0 be adopted, and the first-named director be the registered office contact. (3) [Name] be appointed President and Chief Executive Officer, and [Name] Secretary-Treasurer, each with authority to open and manage corporate bank accounts. (4) The general by-laws be adopted and the corporate minute book established. (5) The corporate seal and common share certificates pattern be approved. APPROVED by the Board of Directors this [Date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and NUANS Report
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry through accredited NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) search houses
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit one to three proposed corporate names to an accredited NUANS provider. Each name must include a legal element such as 'Ltd.', 'Inc.' or 'Corp.' and must be distinctive in Alberta. Obtain the NUANS search report, valid for 90 days, and optionally reserve the approved name.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected, select an alternative name and run a new NUANS search, or incorporate under a numbered Alberta name (e.g., 1234567 Alberta Ltd.) and apply for a name change after incorporation once registry clearance is obtained.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Articles of Incorporation and Statutory Notices
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator, legal counsel and staff of the Alberta Corporate Registry (forms and template guidance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation (Form A-1) setting out the corporate name, authorized share structure with rights and restrictions, first directors and restricted share provisions, if any. Complete the Notice of Registered Office and the Notice of Directors, ensuring the registered office is a physical address within Alberta and each director consents in writing.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act as Director forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry identifies defects, correct the articles and notices and resubmit; if a named director withdraws consent, substitute a qualified director and file a revised Notice of Directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) via ORGOnline or a registered Registry Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Electronically file the completed Articles of Incorporation and statutory notices, pay the incorporation fee of CA$500, and receive the Certificate of Incorporation, Corporate Access Number and approved Articles. The corporation comes into existence on the effective date and time shown on the certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried for fee mismatches or missing consents, pay the deficit or file the missing document within the registry's notice period; otherwise withdraw and re-file a corrected application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Governance - First Board Meeting and Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: First Board of Directors and the corporate secretary / minute book custodian
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the organizational meeting of the first directors and adopt the pro-forma First Board Resolution: accept the share subscription, issue the Class A common shares, adopt the general by-laws, appoint the President, Chief Executive Officer and Secretary-Treasurer, establish the corporate minute book, select the financial year end, and authorize the opening of bank accounts. Record all allotments in the share register.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution and meeting minutes
Shareholder register and corporate minute book
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director or incorporator is unavailable, the sole incorporator may act alone to validate organizational acts; any irregular allotment can be ratified and corrected by an amending resolution of the board.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and Trade Registrations - CRA Business Number, Accounts and SFCR Import Licence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration Online (BRO); Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) for food import licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation with the CRA to obtain the Business Number (BN), the GST/HST account, payroll account where employees will be engaged, and the corporate income tax account. Alberta's 8% corporate income tax is administered by the CRA under a collection agreement, so no separate provincial corporate tax account is required. If the company imports matcha powder into Canada, apply with the CFIA for a Safe Food for Canadians Regulations (SFCR) licence in the 'importing food' category.
required_dossiers: SFCR licence application with preventive control plan (if importing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct CRA linkage errors using form RC245 or by contacting CRA at 1-800-959-5525; CFIA non-compliance notifications are cured by amending and resubmitting the licence application through the My CFIA portal with corrected labelling, traceability and preventive control data.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Occupational and Fire Safety Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal licensing department of the local city (e.g., Calgary or Edmonton), municipal fire marshal, and Alberta Occupational Health and Safety (OHS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a municipal business licence for the registered office and, if applicable, the food-grade storage/warehouse premises. Submit the lease, occupancy permit and proof of incorporation; arrange for a fire safety inspection or complete the municipal fire safety checklist covering extinguishers, exits and alarm systems. If employees are hired, register with WCB-Alberta and complete an OHS hazard assessment. No provincial environmental licence is required for wholesale distribution.
required_dossiers: Proof of WCB-Alberta registration (if any employees)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Remediate any fire or building code deficiencies identified by inspectors, schedule a re-inspection, and supplement the application; if the municipal licence is denied for the storage premise, revise the operational model to office-only and engage a third-party logistics warehouse for the matcha inventory.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No Alberta industrial licensing board applies to wholesale matcha powder distribution; the activity is not designated under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act (EPEA) Activities Designation Regulation. The relevant competent federal food safety authority is the Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) under the Safe Food for Canadians Act.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No provincial industrial operating permit required for import, wholesale and distribution of matcha powder. A federal SFCR Food Import Licence is required if the company imports food into Canada, and a municipal business licence is required for the commercial premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Not Designated. The office, warehousing and distribution activities do not constitute a physical work or manufacturing undertaking requiring a full EIA report or registration under EPEA.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No EPEA wastewater, VOC or effluent discharge limits apply at this scale; general duty to prevent environmental harm under EPEA s. 2 remains applicable. Matcha powder is stored as a food-grade dry powder in sealed packaging; municipal stormwater, solid waste and sewer by-laws govern the leased premises.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Compliance with the Alberta Fire Code is required, including fire extinguishers, unobstructed exits, and fire safety inspection certification for the commercial occupancy permit. A general workplace safety clearance under the Alberta Occupational Health and Safety Act is required for the office and warehouse; no high-hazard civil defense clearance applies. Employers must register with WCB-Alberta before any staff are engaged.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.additional_trade_compliance_note: Although no provincial industrial licence is mandated, the cross-border import of organic matcha powder triggers federal SFCR licensing, CFIA preventive control requirements, Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) importer identification under the Customs Act, and the Safe Food for Canadians labelling rules for organic product claims.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – My Business Account portal (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/e-services-businesses/business-account.html); Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) for export customs clearance
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign corporations must first obtain a statutory Business Number (BN) from the CRA via the Online Business Registry or Form RC22 (Application for Non-Resident Business Account) before engaging in commercial activity in Alberta. Registration must be accompanied by a GST/HST account (Form RC1) if taxable supplies are made in Canada. The BN serves as the TIN for federal and Alberta tax compliance. Non-residents are advised to appoint a Canadian agent for service of process.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists under Canadian federal or Alberta law. Entity classification for foreign and domestic corporations is determined by CRA administrative rules and applicable tax treaties. Available narrow elections include: GST/HST closely related corporation election under Section 156 of the Excise Tax Act; discretionary joint election under Section 61 for a supply of taxable real property; and Section 216 elective filing for Canadian-source rental income. No hybrid mismatch election is separately recognized.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 gross annual taxable supplies in Canada as determined over the current and previous four calendar quarters (small supplier threshold); non-residents deriving taxable revenue from Canadian commercial activity may be required to register regardless of threshold
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No federal mandate for real-time e-invoicing, fiscal stamping, or government clearance of invoices. Invoices must contain mandatory GST/HST information prescribed under Section 223 of the Excise Tax Act and Input Tax Credit Information Regulations. GST/HST returns must be filed electronically via NETFILE when revenue exceeds thresholds. Export transactions require electronic submission of customs documentation through CBSA eManifest / Canadian Export Reporting (CCLDP) in the prescribed format.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating for exported matcha powder requires that the exporter holds documentary evidence of physical removal from Canada, title to the goods passes to a foreign purchaser, and the goods are exported within a reasonable period (normally within 12 months) under Excise Tax Act Section 39. Services performed directly on the goods or ancillary to export may zero-rate under Division IV Regulations. Foreign purchasers must be non-residents and the goods must not be returned to Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading (Ocean or Air Waybill)
Inward Remittance Certificate (proof of FX repatriation, where required)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess within four years (or longer in cases of misrepresentation or fraud), deny zero-rating status, and apply 5% GST plus interest. Penalties for false statements, deliberate evasion, or overclaimed refunds under Section 280.08 of Excise Tax Act and Sections 285/288 can amount to the greater of CAD 100 and 25% of the net tax evaded. Criminal prosecution under Section 239 ETA may result in fines up to CAD 500,000 and/or imprisonment. Retrospective clawback of input tax refunds is enforceable through civil reassessment and revenue prosecution.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (central monetary authority). The foreign exchange control framework in Canada is administered by the Department of Finance Canada, with day-to-day enforcement under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), supervised by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC). No exchange-control statute imposes prior approval on foreign exchange transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible; both current and capital account transactions are freely settled without exchange-control license. Cross-border wire transfers and foreign currency purchases in excess of CAD 10,000 are reported by financial institutions to FINTRAC. Profit and dividend remittances are unrestricted, subject to Canada Revenue Agency withholdings (Part XIII tax on payments to non-residents, unless reduced by treaty) and corporate compliance. No anti-avoidance 'forced conversion' applies to export receipts.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or mandatory conversion of export proceeds applies in Canada. Exporters may retain funds in any currency for an indefinite period, or convert to CAD at commercial bank rates. Exporters must maintain full documentation (customs declarations via CBSA, commercial invoices, and settlement records) for six years. FINTRAC reporting thresholds (e.g., cross-border transfer of CAD 10,000 or more) remain applicable.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore electronic money institutions (EMIs) and global fintech payment platforms (Wise, Payoneer) are not licensed as Canadian banks but may operate as money service businesses (MSBs) where activities occur in Canada, requiring FINTRAC MSB registration. Their multi-currency accounts and lower transaction fees provide medium feasibility as supplemental rails for unit disbursements, but they generally do not offer formal overnight liquidity, trade finance facilities, or a stable 'settlement hub'. For sustained cross-border procurement, a tier-1 Canadian bank account is mandatory.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In Alberta, tier-1 banks permit remote corporate account opening when the applicant submits Articles of Incorporation, an organizational resolution, a register of directors and individuals with significant control (ISC), and evidence of due diligence on beneficial owners. In practice, a physical or video KYC interview is required for designated signatories and directors; a remote interview is acceptable if identity is verified through notarized documents or a Canadian legal/accounting professional. Non-resident directors typically need a notarized copy of a passport and a written instruction to the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency cross-border wires with multiple third-party payor/payee configurations not referenced in the underlying trade agreement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete commercial contract chain (purchase order, pro-forma invoice, final invoice), quality/certificate analysis for matcha (food safety certificate, organic certification), customs declarations (cargo control list from CBSA), transport documents (bill of lading / air waybill), and bank statement evidence showing that all payees/payors are named in the transaction records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity caused by layered corporate structures or nominees in high-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full shareholding registry, register of individuals with significant control (ISC Registry), corporate organizational chart, notarized passport of directors/UBOs, and a legal opinion letter explaining ownership structure and source of wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Invoice anomalies, including over/under-invoicing or invoicing from a shell entity in a non-cooperative jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent product valuation certificates (lab testing and organic certification), inspection company (SGS/Bureau Veritas) report, prior trade history and banking transaction patterns, and supplier due diligence (business registration, tax status, operational address).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection to CA_CORP (Alberta) arrives via SWIFT MT103 from the parent shareholder (or investor) to the bank's commercial account. Routing must include full remitter and beneficiary names (not merely account numbers), the corporate identification (Company's incorporation number), and the bank's BIC code. For FINTRAC, the purpose should be stated as 'Inbound Investment / Capital Call' or, if procurement finance, 'Payment for Import Settlement'. The bank should be pre-notified with the capital contribution agreement, a board resolution from the applicant, and an asset/liability schedule to accelerate verification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For settlement with the Japanese matcha supplier (or other suppliers), the primary rails are: (1) SWIFT MT103 for telegraphic transfer where the supplier accepts an open account; (2) a commercial letter of credit (LC) issued by the Canadian bank under UCP600, confirmed by the seller's bank, for large-value and single-shipment purchase; and (3) check/documentary collection when commercially prudent. SC packing invoices and exchange rates are used for CAD/JPY conversion. The bank may request a UCP600 version and charge a confirmation fee, which can be negotiated into the vendor's terms.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forward Contracts (deliverable CAD/JPY or CAD/USD), maturities commonly up to 12 months
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) only for currencies with no CAD deliverability (e.g., certain Asian and emerging-market ccy pairs), restricted to hedging actual trade exposure
Cross-Currency Swaps (CAD vs. trade currency) for flipping debt/funding cash flows
FX Options (plain vanilla) for optional hedging for high-volatility tender periods

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary date of incorporation (not fiscal year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a CAD 100 penalty surcharge; default for at least one year triggers a Notice of Intent to Dissolve published in the Alberta Gazette with a 120-day cure period, followed by administrative dissolution under ABCA s.214; reinstatement requires arrears filing plus fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA) - applicable to federally incorporated corporations only
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days of the anniversary date of incorporation or amalgamation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No late fee is imposed, but failure to file for one year permits the Director to publish a notice in the Canada Gazette with a 120-day cure period, followed by dissolution under CBCA s.212; revival requires payment of the prescribed fee and filing of all outstanding annual returns.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal and Alberta corporate income tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Business Returns Directorate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end (e.g., June 30 for a December 31 year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; repeat failures trigger higher minimum penalties; CRA may issue a demand to file, assess tax on an estimated basis, and charge statutory interest on arrears.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies to distributing (public) corporations under CBCA s.156 and ABCA s.150/151; a private non-distributing corporation may waive the auditor each year by unanimous shareholder resolution. No revenue or asset threshold in Alberta law triggers a statutory audit for a closely held corporation; lenders or commercial counterparties may nonetheless require an audit or review engagement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is required for publicly accountable enterprises; Canadian ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook Part II) is the default framework for private enterprises and is appropriate for a closely held matcha powder distribution company.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For ABCA corporations, the Alberta Annual Return re-certifies registered office and director particulars; Alberta's beneficial ownership transparency amendments (2022) require an internal register of individuals with significant control (ISC), but UBO particulars are not yet collected on the annual return. For CBCA corporations, the ISC register must be maintained under s.21.1 CBCA, updated within 15 days of any shareholding change, and confirmed as accurate on each federal annual return; phased filing of beneficial ownership data with the federal registry applies.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (minutes and resolutions of meetings)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 110-300 per year (CAD 150-400) for a commercial registered office and corporate agent in Alberta
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000-15,000 (CAD 8,000-20,000) for a full independent audit; review engagement typically USD 2,200-4,500 (CAD 3,000-6,000); audit may be waived for a private non-distributing corporation

stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions
